newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTH AFRICA RESERVE BANK REVISES CURRENT ACCOUNT DATA.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH AFRICA RESERVE BANK REVISES CURRENT ACCOUNT DATA.

text.p: The Reserve Bank has revised its current account figures for the last four years to account for gold exports not previously taken into consideration, an official told Reuters on Thursday.
He said 1995 current account deficit had been revised to 10.157 billion rand compared with a previously published figure of 12.656 billion rand for the same period.
Data for 1994, 1993, and 1992 was also revised, albeit to a lesser extent.
The official said the figures had been revised after the central bank had found that certain gold exports were not included previously. He did not elaborate further.
Net gold exports from 1992 to the first quarter of 1996 were all revised upwards.
Other adjustments were also made to the 1995 figures, including import and export statistics.
"1995 was a major revision of the whole of the balance of payments," the official said.
Edward Osborn, strategic economist at Edey Rogers & Co, has recently questioned the figures, saying that the Bank's definitions of gold exports have ommitted forward sales.
